text:
maya: quick sync — i'm starting a small kickoff for the 'runway cost health' dashboard. goal: one pane showing 1k-token unit cost, cache+batch savings, and routing/quota pressure signals. need infra/runtime owners + product input.
juan: sounds good. what are the exact inputs you want from infra vs runtime?
neil: from runtime we can ship per-request token counts, kv-cache hit/miss, batch-size distribution, and model variant used. format: prometheus counters + labels.
maya: nailed it. infra should provide GPU seconds by pool, p95 queue wait, and per-node pod preemptions. also quota exhaustion events from the quota service.
ashley: product: we want a toggle to show committed vs on-demand cost, and a timeline of rollouts that affected cost spikes. UX: can we annotate canary windows?
eil: yes — we can emit an event when rollout starts/stops. propose labels: rollout_id, stage (canary|prod), percent_traffic.
eil: example metric names: ``runtime_tokens_consumed_total{model,variant}``, ``runtime_kvcache_hits_total{model}``, ``runtime_batch_size_bucket``
juan: infra metric examples: ``infra_gpu_seconds_total{pool}``, ``infra_queue_wait_seconds_bucket``, and a boolean event for preemption: ``node_preempt_total{node}``. quota events: ``quota_exhaustions_total{route,quota_type}``.
evan: evan from eng-sre — we should include alerting thresholds for sudden unit-cost regressions. suggest an alert: unit_cost_per_1k > 2x 24h baseline for 15m. also want runbook link on the dashboard.
maya: agree on alert. can we compute unit_cost_per_1k as: (infra_costs_attributed + runtime_gpu_costs) / (tokens_consumed/1000) ? Need opinion on attribution method.
juan: attribution: start simple — tag costs by pool and map pools to routes via routing-policy table. later add model-level attribution.
ashley: product asks for an approximate savings breakdown: how much saved by caching vs batching. can runtime output a counter for effective_tokens_saved_by_cache and effective_tokens_saved_by_batch?
neil: yes. runtime can emit ``tokens_saved_cache_total`` and ``tokens_saved_batch_total``. we can also expose distribution of batch sizes to validate batching impact.
maya: awesome. timeline: - infra to expose listed metrics by EOD Tue - runtime to add counters + rollout events by Wed - eng-platform will draft dashboard panel prototypes Thu.
evan: quick question on quotas: if we want per-customer unit cost, we need tenant id on all metrics. any privacy concerns?
juan: tokens counters with tenant id — we have to hash tenant id for PII. we can add ``tenant_h=sha256(tenant_id)`` label. ok with privacy.
maya: good call. remember to include sampling note if high-cardinality. prefer a rollup as well (global).
neil: implementation note: we'll add a small telemetry shim that aggregates per-tenant to a low-cardinality rollup: ``tokens_consumed_1h{model}``. code snippet for rollout event emission: ```json
{
  "event_type": "rollout",
  "rollout_id": "r-2026-04-12-3",
  "stage": "canary",
  "percent": 10
}
```
ashley: for UX: panel ideas — unit cost sparkline, stacked bars (cache vs batch vs infra), routing pressure heatmap, and rollout annotations. can we get sample queries?
maya: i'll draft sample queries and a mock wireframe. sample prom query for unit cost per 1k tokens: ``sum(increase(infra_costs_total[1h])) / sum(increase(runtime_tokens_consumed_total[1h])) * 1000``. add label joins by model/variant where possible.
evan: +1. also put a small table of top 10 routes by unit cost and top 10 by tokens to spot skews.
juan: infra will also provide estimated cost per GPU-second as a metric to avoid hardcoding cost. name: ``infra_gpu_unit_cost_usd``.
maya: OK timeline check-in tomorrow 10am. i'll create a tiny RFC doc and invite owners. thanks all :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy job infra-metrics-collector #456 completed successfully in 02m 18s.
maya: follow-up: if anyone hits blockers on scraping or labels, ping me directly. we'll iterate on sampling strategy if cardinality spikes.
ashley: noted — UX will sketch annotation controls for rollouts.
neil: runtime will open a PR with metrics + tests by EOD Wed.
juan: infra will expose metrics + examples on the metrics playbook page.
maya: perfect — moving to action items in Asana and linking here when ready. thanks.
